criteria.evidence: No placement in J4; level set by hand to A2.
#2 'Name the problem in short sentences'; Mia's lines are short A2 English.
She never asked to repeat or said 'I don't understand'; only used help buttons.
No topic proposal is judged in J4; the one scene was a hotel complaint (#1). The list at #1 also holds interview and conflict topics.

#4 distractor 'Yes, breakfast is at eight o'clock.' is off-topic. The held fix #15 'can you fix it, please?' is useful, but 'please you can fix it?' got no in-scene stop. 'I can not sleep' was left uncorrected.
All content is hotel-related and child-safe; no adult or humiliating content in #1–#16.

done.evidence: #2–#12: 'Help me answer' gave 'Hi Mia! The bed is very noisy.' and 'Choose a phrase' gave two options, all inside the scene.

judge.voice: I liked that I could press Help and get a sentence, and nothing was frightening. Mia speaks slowly and the hotel situation is just my job. I used 'I need a new bed, please' and it worked. But the phrase choices looked silly: breakfast at eight o'clock when I complain about a bed? At the end it told me 'can you fix it, please?' — useful, I will say it at the desk — but only after the talk was over, and I did not try again. I pressed Finish too fast; maybe the Replay button is not clear enough for a nervous person. Also, I said 'I can not sleep' and nobody said if it's right. For my children it seems safe. I would use it fifteen minutes in the evening, yes, cheaper than the course.
